_about: Pirates and the high seas: ships, crews, ports, treasure, storms and the navies that hunt them. Story axes for story_gen.py. Each axis is rolled on its own; an entry is a string (weight 1) or {v, w, decay}. All text is our own.

ship: a stolen navy sloop still flying false colours
a leaky junk with a red sail patched twice
a fast schooner built for smuggling
a captured merchant galleon too slow to run
a prau out of the spice islands with twin outriggers
a whaler turned raider, still smelling of oil
a hulk with too many guns and too few hands
captain_want: a pardon and a quiet farm ashore
revenge on the admiral who hanged her brother
a crown on a pirate island of their own
enough gold to buy back a sold-off family
to find the island on a dead man's chart
to be feared in every port of the strait
to outrun a curse that follows the ship
to free the slaves in the hold of a rival
prize: a treasure fleet sailing home late in the season
a sunken temple bell made of solid gold
a cargo of pepper worth a duke's ransom
a governor's daughter who wants to be taken
a chest of pearls buried on a sandbar
a stolen royal seal that can forge any letter
a wreck in the reefs off the andaman coast
the chart to a hidden anchorage
port: a lawless free port built on old hulls
a colonial fort town with a hanging dock
a stilt village in the mangroves of the gulf
a pearl-diving harbour run by an old widow
a smugglers' cove under white limestone cliffs
a neutral island where every flag drinks together
a trading city at a river mouth, full of spies
a burned port nobody is supposed to visit
hunter: a navy frigate under a captain with something to prove
a pirate hunter paid by the head
a former crewmate who sold them out
a rival captain who wants the same prize
a sultan's war fleet guarding the strait
a ghost ship that keeps appearing at dusk
a bounty posted in every port they need
sea_danger: a storm season arriving a month early
a calm that leaves them drifting with no water
a reef that moves with the tides
a monsoon wind that will not let them turn
a sea serpent the old hands swear is real
fog so thick they hear the other ship first

cliches: the treasure map with an x
a parrot on the captain's shoulder
the drunk captain who is secretly brilliant
